facts.statement: The source has doc_ref D4.
The source title is "Difficult diagnosis and genetic analysis of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: a case report".
The source URL is https://bmcmedgenet.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12881-018-0543-7.
Because of the rarity of FOP, most patients are misdiagnosed to have unnecessary biopsies performed [6, 8, 9].
Most patients are misdiagnosed to undergo intramuscular injections or surgical excisions of ectopic bone [6, 8, 9].
Intramuscular injections or surgical excisions of ectopic bone can trigger episodes of explosive heterotopic ossification [6, 8, 9].
It has recently been shown that FOP is caused by heterozygous activating mutations in ACVR1/ALK2 [10,11,12].
ACVR1/ALK2 is activin A receptor, type I/activin-like kinase 2.
ACVR1/ALK2 is a bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) type I receptor [10,11,12].
Based on these findings, DNA sequence analysis of ACVR1/ALK2 of suspected patients can confirm the diagnosis of FOP, thus avoiding misdiagnosis and mismanagement [13].
In the current case report, the authors managed a sixteen-year-old male patient with the classic features of FOP by making a genetic analysis.
The authors presented a deep insight into the diagnosis of this rare disorder.
The current case report was presented in accordance with the CARE guidelines.
A sixteen-year-old male patient was brought to the authors' emergency room with the complaints of pain and swelling in his upper back.
A biopsy had been performed in the patient's upper back two months before.
At the age of 9, the patient developed tender stiffness of his shoulders and neck.
Over the next 4 years, the patient experienced multiple similar swellings on the upper back.
Subsequently, the movement of the shoulders and neck was limited.
Subsequently, masses grew progressively.
The patient went to the specialists at some local hospitals for examination and treatment.
The specialists managed the patient without making a confirmative diagnosis.
Two months before, one of the doctors at the local hospitals arranged a biopsy for the patient.
The results of the pathological examination only revealed that the mass was heterotopic ossification.
The cause of the heterotopic ossification was unclear.
FOP is a rare disorder.
